blog/tasbeeh-counter.description: How to use a digital tasbeeh counter on your phone: a target of 33, 99, 100 or free, the after-prayer tasbeeh and today's total.
blog/tasbeeh-counter.h1: How to use an online tasbeeh counter
blog/tasbeeh-counter.body:
It is not always easy to keep count while doing tasbeeh. A digital tasbeeh counter on your phone makes it simple: you just keep tapping and the count rises by itself.

How to use it

  1. Choose a target: 33, 99, 100 or free.
  2. Tap the big button each time you say the dhikr shown.
  3. When the target is reached the tool tells you and moves to the next dhikr by itself.
  4. Press “Reset” to take the count back to zero.

Choosing a target

  • 33 / 99 / 100: each dhikr that many times, then the next one appears.
  • Free: no limit; keep going as long as you like.

The after-prayer tasbeeh

A hadith mentions saying SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times and Allahu Akbar 34 times after prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim). Reports can differ slightly in detail, so check the full order in a reliable book or with a scholar. In the tool, choose a target of 33, then switch to “Free” for the third dhikr to count up to 34.

Masnoon duas and wazaif

The same page has masnoon duas (for waking, eating, travelling and more) and a few well-known wazaif, with meaning and source. To confirm the Arabic text, check a reliable book such as Hisn al-Muslim.

Today's total and the screen

The tool shows today's total count, and the “Keep screen awake” button (where your phone allows it) stops the screen turning off while you count. Your count is saved only in your phone's browser.
blog/tasbeeh-counter.ctaText: Start counting tasbeeh on your phone now.

blog/unit-converter.title: How to Convert cm to Feet and Inches and Plot Area to Marla | Mufeed Tools
blog/unit-converter.description: A simple way to convert height from centimetres to feet and inches and to work out plot area in square feet, square yards, marla and kanal, with an example.
blog/unit-converter.h1: How to convert cm to feet and inches and plot area to marla
blog/unit-converter.body:
A height, a room length or a plot measurement often comes in one unit when you need another. If someone is 182 cm tall, you may want to know how that is in feet and inches. Our unit converter and plot area tool does all of this in one place.

Basic measures worth remembering

  • 1 inch = 2.54 cm
  • 1 foot = 12 inches = 30.48 cm
  • 1 yard (gaz) = 3 feet = 36 inches
  • 1 metre = 100 cm = 3.28084 feet
  • 1 square yard = 9 square feet
  • 1 kanal = 20 marla

Converting height to feet and inches

  1. Choose “Centimetre” as the unit.
  2. Type the value, for example 182.
  3. The “Height in feet + inches” box shows the result at once: 5 ft 11.65 in.
  4. The result also appears below in every other unit.

How plot area is worked out

Enter the lengths of the four walls in feet and inches. The tool averages the front and back walls for the length and the left and right walls for the width, then multiplies the two.

An example

Suppose the front and back walls are 45 ft each and the left and right walls are 90 ft each. The area is 4,050 sq ft, which is 450 sq yd. On a marla of 225 sq ft that is 18 marla and 0.9 kanal.

How many square feet is a marla?

The tool uses 225 sq ft, but some areas and schemes use 250 or 272.25 sq ft. Choose your standard from the list. On the 272.25 standard the same plot is about 14.88 marla.

An important note

This method averages opposite walls, so for an irregular plot the result is approximate. For buying, selling, registration or any legal matter, rely on a licensed surveyor or the local revenue office.

blog/qr-code.title: QR Code Guide: Scanning, Account Details and Printing for a Shop | Mufeed Tools
blog/qr-code.description: How to scan a QR code, how to make one for a link, WhatsApp, Wi-Fi or account details, and how to print a poster for your shop.
blog/qr-code.h1: QR code guide: scanning, account details and printing for a shop
blog/qr-code.body:
A QR code is a small square that hides a link, a number or some text. Our QR code generator makes one with the colours and logo you choose.

How to scan a QR code

Open your phone camera and point it at the code, then tap the notification that appears. A link opens the website, a WhatsApp code opens the chat, and a Wi-Fi code offers to join the network.

What kinds of QR can you make?

  • Link / text: a website or social page.
  • WhatsApp: a chat with your number, optionally with a ready message.
  • Wi-Fi: a guest joins without typing the password.
  • vCard: name, number and email saved as a contact.
  • Account details: name, bank and account number as plain text.

The account-details QR: an important difference

This QR only shows what you typed, and a customer can read it and copy the number. It is not an official payment QR issued by a bank. To pay, use the “Scan QR” option in your bank or wallet app with a QR issued by the bank, and for an official merchant QR contact your bank.

Print a poster for your shop

  1. Choose the type and fill in the details in the tool.
  2. Press “Print poster” and choose A4 or A5.
  3. Print it, laminate it and place it on the counter where customers can see it.
  4. Scan it with your own phone before using it.

To keep scanning easy

  • Keep the QR dark and the background light.
  • Keep any logo small and simple.
  • Do not make the text very long.
blog/qr-code.ctaText: Make your own QR code now, free.
